ledger.why: the Building or Devotion effect on the ending page; the Isolan visitor is text only

items.text: the village leader with an enormous nose
a healer holding what looks like a dead fish
a builder standing beside a collapsed hut
a researcher surrounded by crooked numbers
two children arguing over a coconut
an elder asleep beneath a tree
a ceremonial dancer with an unfortunately large backside
The carving is a symbol of strength, and the exaggerated feature is considered an honor in the visitor's tradition.
The figure depicts a famous old story, not the person the villager assumed.
The visitor admits (visitor.he/she) is simply terrible at faces.
The visitor intended a gentle joke and apologizes when told it caused embarrassment.
The villagers discover the carving has a meaningful history and decide to display it.
The recipient admits (recipient.he/she) doesn't want it displayed. The group respects that choice.
The misunderstanding is resolved with a quiet conversation.
The visitor apologizes sincerely and offers to remake it.
The visitor is hurt that the gift was misunderstood. Both sides take time to explain their feelings.
The recipient realizes (recipient.he/she) jumped to conclusions, and apologizes in return.
Neither side agrees about whether the joke was appropriate, but they part respectfully.
The villagers carve a friendly caricature of the visitor. The visitor laughs until (visitor.he/she) cries.
The return gift is much more insulting than intended. The villagers immediately apologize.
The visitors propose an annual exchange of deliberately terrible portraits. Both communities agree.
The neutral judge from the woodworking contest is invited to decide whose carving is worse. The judge refuses to get involved.
The carving is displayed with a note explaining its meaning.
The gift is accepted privately, without a public display.
The visitor returns another day with a revised carving.
The recipient and visitor laugh about the misunderstanding over a shared meal.
They do not become close friends, but each has learned something about the other's perspective.

intro.name: The carving
intro.text: An Isolan neighbor arrives with a gift for the village: a carefully carved wooden figure depicting {A}.

question.name: A joke?
question.text:
The visitor looks delighted. (Recipient) looks horrified.
"Is this supposed to be a joke?" (recipient.he/she) asks.
The Isolan visitor {looks confused|smiles proudly|realizes something is wrong but cannot guess what}.

choices.label: ACCEPT IT POLITELY AND DISCUSS IT LATER.
EXPLAIN WHY IT MIGHT BE HURTFUL.
